basis: Carcinoma arising in intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts, all within the hepatic axis.
Direct injury to multiple peripheral nerves; underlying causes vary and do not establish an immune mechanism for the umbrella concept.
Defining skeletal dysplasia; oral malformations include cleft palate in 75% and dental agenesis in 50%; ventricular septal defect in 50%. Eye appearance alone does not establish damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with cortical malformations and seizures; visual impairment in 2/7 is below 30%; isolated additional findings do not establish common organ damage.
Inherited skin fragility; characteristic enamel hypoplasia and oral mucosal blistering affect most patients. Airway and renal disease vary by subtype.
Infantile generalized dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal muscle contraction does not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Intellectual disability, seizures and small hands/feet define the syndrome; cataract/glaucoma in about 50% and cleft palate in about 33% support eye and oral involvement.
Hemolytic sickling disorder; renal medullary dysfunction and ischemic bone injury affect >30%. Separately diagnosed retinopathy, gallstones and infections are excluded.
Disease of the gingiva; gums and oral mucosa belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Intradural spinal arachnoid cysts occupy the central nervous system and can compress the spinal cord or nerve roots.
Nonsyndromic inherited cataract with microcornea; disease is confined to the eye.
Sebaceous gland carcinoma arises in skin or ocular adnexal glands; eyelid origin is common. Metastatic sites are not inherent organ labels.
Infantile myofibroblastic tumors characteristically arise in skin, subcutis and skeletal soft tissues; common visceral damage is not established for this subtype.
Acquired excess of circulating red blood cells; causes and vascular complications do not establish additional common organ damage.
Glycosylation disorder defined by myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy; intellectual disability and stroke-like CNS dysfunction are frequent (30-79%).
Congenital absence of the tricuspid valve with right ventricular hypoplasia and associated cardiac or great-vessel malformations.
Myosin-storage skeletal myopathy with weakness and structural muscle abnormalities; reduced vital capacity occurs in 25% and does not establish direct lung disease.
Cortical, brainstem and cerebellar malformations cause neurodevelopmental dysfunction; common ocular motor abnormalities do not establish direct eye damage.
Hamartomatous polyp arising predominantly in gastrointestinal mucosa; nasopharyngeal and urinary locations are rare.
Gonococcal infection of the fallopian tubes; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism qualifies.
Neurologic loss of awareness of one's own impairments, classified as an agnosia.
Umbrella of FLNB-related skeletal dysplasias; bone and joint malformations are shared, while additional organ findings vary across subtypes.
Congenital herniation of intracranial contents through a parietal skull defect; neural tissue and the cranial bone defect define the condition.
Classical complement immunodeficiency; lupus, glomerulonephritis, thyroiditis and hepatitis are associated separate diseases without qualifying organ frequencies.
Intraneuronal neuroserpin inclusions cause progressive neuronal loss, encephalopathy, dementia and seizures; no common direct extra-neural damage is established.
